identity.title: Single breath count (count aloud on one full inspiration; <20 signals weak respiratory muscles)

technique.how: Patient sits upright, takes a maximal inspiration and counts aloud from 1 at about 2 counts per second (metronome or audio app at 2 Hz) in a normal speaking voice until the breath runs out. Record the highest number reached; take the best of 2-3 attempts. Repeat serially (e.g. every 4-6 h) in neuromuscular patients.
technique.prerequisites: Alert patient who can phonate and follow commands; count in the patient's own language.
technique.contraindications: Not interpretable with severe bulbar weakness, aphonia, or in intubated patients.

interpretation.positive_finding: A low count signals reduced vital capacity: in GBS, SBC <=5 predicted need for mechanical ventilation (sens 0.906, spec 0.952); SBC <=25 by telephone flagged MG exacerbation (sens 0.80); SBC <=21 predicted VC <20 mL/kg (sens 0.944, spec 0.766).
interpretation.negative_finding: SBC >19 had 95% sensitivity for ruling out need for mechanical ventilation in GBS; healthy young adults count 31-49. A single normal count does not exclude later decline - trend it.
interpretation.pitfalls: Counting speed, language, posture and vocal effort change the number, and cutoffs (5 to 32) vary across studies; bulbar weakness and dyspnea from another cause lower the count without respiratory-muscle weakness.
interpretation.changes_what: SBC <20 or falling trend: measure FVC/NIF, ABG, and move toward ICU-level monitoring; SBC <=5 in GBS: prepare for intubation. High stable count: continue ward monitoring.

estimates.target_condition: Need for intubation/mechanical ventilation in Guillain-Barre syndrome; SBC <=5 (2 Hz paced)
estimates.population: 94 GBS patients with serial SBC and ABG-based modified intubation criteria (tertiary neurology unit, India)
estimates.reference_standard: ABG-defined intubation criteria (PaO2 <60 with PaCO2 >50, or pH <7.3)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.906/(1-0.952) = 18.9; LR- = (1-0.906)/0.952 = 0.10; from reported sensitivity 90.6% and specificity 95.2%
estimates.quote: At SBC 5, need for MV could be predicted with a sensitivity of 90.6% and specificity of 95.2%.

estimates.target_condition: Need for mechanical ventilation in Guillain-Barre syndrome; SBC >19 as rule-out
estimates.population: 68 GBS patients (Kanikannan 2014, as summarized in the systematic review)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical need for mechanical ventilation during admission
estimates.quote: SBCT>19 had sensitivity of 95% in ruling out the need for mechanical ventilation

estimates.target_condition: Myasthenia gravis exacerbation; nurse-administered telephonic SBC <=25
estimates.population: 45 telephone calls from MG patients reporting worsening symptoms (single-center retrospective pilot)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of MG exacerbation after evaluation
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.80/(1-0.60) = 2.0; LR- = (1-0.80)/0.60 = 0.33; from reported sensitivity 80% and specificity 60%
estimates.quote: the nurse-administered telephonic SBCT had a positive predictive value of 71%, sensitivity of 80%, and specificity of 60%

estimates.population: Patients with a variety of diseases (Escossio 2019, as summarized in the systematic review)
estimates.quote: SBCT of 21 or less had a sensitivity and specificity of 94.4% and 76.62% for VC <20 ml/kg

sources.citation: Bhandari SK, Bist A, Ghimire A. Single breath count test and its applications in clinical practice: a systematic review. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2024;86(4):2096-2101.
Kalita J, Kumar M, Misra UK. Serial single breath count is a reliable tool for monitoring respiratory functions in Guillain-Barre Syndrome. J Clin Neurosci. 2020;72:50-56.
Kukulka K, Gummi RR, Govindarajan R. A telephonic single breath count test for screening of exacerbations of myasthenia gravis: a pilot study. Muscle Nerve. 2020;62(2):258-261.

Elsheikh B, Arnold WD, Gharibshahi S, Reynolds J, Freimer M, Kissel JT. Correlation of single-breath count test and neck flexor muscle strength with spirometry in myasthenia gravis. Muscle Nerve. 2016;53(1):134-136.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not substitute for spirometry (FVC/NIF) when it is available, and do not interpret in patients with severe bulbar weakness, aphonia or non-neuromuscular dyspnea.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: SBC <20, a fall of >20% over 24 h, or SBC <=5 in GBS/MG indicates impending respiratory failure: obtain FVC/NIF and ABG and involve ICU before hypoxemia appears (SpO2 lags).
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Reproducibility depends on paced counting (2 Hz) and standardized voice/posture; the systematic review notes cutoffs varied 5-32 across studies because methods differed, and no healthy reference range is established beyond 31-49 in young adults.

extraction_notes: Systematic review PMC10990392 full text was read (Results text and Table 3); it is a narrative systematic review without pooling, so each entry is a single-study estimate. Kalita 2020 and Kukulka 2020 numbers were confirmed against their own PubMed abstracts; Kanikannan 2014 (J Crit Care, PMID 24378177 found by search but not fetched) and Escossio 2019 estimates are taken from the review's Table 3 and cite the review. Elsheikh 2016 (correlation with FVC/NIF, no cutoff) is cited for the MG technique validity without an estimate. The '<20' threshold in the title is a common clinical convention supported by the Kanikannan >19 rule-out cutoff, not by a pooled estimate.
